transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, but I'm here because... well, for a long time now, my sleep has just been kind of broken. 

I try not to complain too much, but I just fall into bed completely exhausted at the end of the day. But then I can't seem to stay asleep. I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm usually up way before my alarm even goes off, just feeling like I never really rested at all. 

Is that... does that make sense? I just thought maybe I should finally come in and ask someone about it, if that's alright.
Do you feel tired or fatigued during the day?

Well, I mean... I guess everyone gets a little tired, right? I really hope I don't sound lazy saying this, but... yes, I do get pretty worn out. 

By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients for the day and come back to help out at home, my body just feels so... heavy. It's silly, but even just sitting down to chart my notes or, um, trying to fold a basket of laundry... it can just feel like it's almost too much to push through. 

I always try to keep a smile on for my clients, of course, and I really do try to push past it. But... is it normal to feel that drained from just everyday things? I feel like I should be able to handle it better, you know?
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm answering this right, but I wouldn't really say I'm an anxious person. 

I try very hard not to be a worrywart, you know? I just try to take things as they come so I don't stress anyone else out. I mean, sure, I worry a little bit about the normal things, like making sure my clients are comfortable or getting the bills paid on time, but nothing out of the ordinary, I don't think. 

I hope that's okay? I mostly just feel... well, drained, like I mentioned earlier. But not really nervous or panicked or anything like that. Is that what you meant?
Do you feel like you're getting restful sleep when you do sleep?

Well, um... I guess I kind of mentioned it earlier, but no, not really. I mean, I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I don't want to waste your time. 

But yeah, even when I do sleep, it's just... broken. Like I said, I fall into bed so exhausted, but then I just wake up to every little creak or sound in the house. And then I'm awake before my alarm even goes off, and I just feel... well, like I haven't really rested at all. 

I try to just push through it and start my day, but... I don't know, is it normal to wake up feeling that way? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you find yourself lacking motivation to do things you normally enjoy?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful for the good things in my life, because I really am blessed. But, um... yes, I suppose I do struggle with that a little bit. 

It's just... most days, it feels like the color has sort of gone out of things? I hope that doesn't sound too dramatic. Like, even when I'm sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, which I usually love, or... or looking at art that I used to really enjoy, I just feel kind of flat. And sometimes, I actually have to work really hard not to tear up, and there's not even a clear reason for it. 

I always try to keep it together so I don't ruin the mood for anyone else, you know? But... is it okay that I feel that way? I just feel terrible admitting it, like I'm not appreciating my family enough.
Do you often feel sad?

Oh, um... yes. I guess I sort of just spilled all of that out a second ago, didn't I? I'm so sorry, I hope I didn't mess up the order of your questions. 

But yes, I suppose that is what it is. Sadness. Like I was just saying, it's that feeling that the color has just completely gone out of everything. And the crying... it happens right in the middle of Sunday dinner, or when I'm looking at art I usually love. I just have to work so, so hard to swallow it down and not tear up, especially since there's really no clear reason for it. 

I really don't want to make anyone else sad or bring down the room, you know? So I just try to keep smiling through it. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm giving you what you need.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... it's been quite a while now. I'd say... a little over two years? 

It kind of started right around the time my mother-in-law moved in with us. I mean, please don't get me wrong, I love her dearly and I'm so glad we can be there to help her. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about having her in our home! Family is so important, and I know it's a blessing to have her with us. 

But... yes, that just seems to be when this all began, a little over two years ago. I hope it's okay that I brought that up... I don't want to sound selfish or like I'm blaming her for anything. Does that give you the timeline you needed?
Have you experienced any periods of feeling better in the past two years, or has it been a constant feeling of sadness?

Well, um... I really try to focus on the positive days, you know? I don't want to sound like I'm just miserable all the time, because I'm really not. 

But... if I'm being completely honest... I don't think there's been a time where it completely went away? I mean, there are definitely days where it's easier to push through and get things done, and I always make sure to keep up with my patients and everything at home. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm letting my responsibilities slide. 

But that underlying feeling, that sort of grayness... I don't think it's ever fully lifted in these past couple of years. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terribly pessimistic. I really do try to look on the bright side. Is that... does that answer your question properly?
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide in the past two years?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. 

I mean, I know things have been hard, and I've been feeling so down, but... I would never do something like that. I have my husband, and my mother-in-law to take care of, and my patients rely on me so much. I could never just... leave them like that. It would be so terribly selfish of me, wouldn't it? 

I just want to get back to being myself so I can be a better help to everyone. I really hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who would just give up. I'm trying very hard, I promise. Is... is it normal that you have to ask that? I hope I didn't say something earlier that made you worry I might do something awful.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or weight over the past two years?

Well, um... I really try to make sure my husband and my mother-in-law eat well, you know? I always cook for them. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting the cooking or anything like that. 

But for myself... I guess I just haven't been quite as hungry lately. It's nothing serious, really! I just... I don't have much of an appetite anymore. I mostly just end up picking at whatever I make for them, or maybe I'll just grab a piece of toast after my shift is over. I'm still eating, I promise, I just don't need as much. 

I have noticed my clothes are hanging a bit looser lately, even though I haven't been trying to lose weight. I hope that's not too concerning? I really am trying to take care of myself, I just... the hunger isn't really there. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Has this feeling of sadness and lack of motivation been continuous over the past two years, or have you had periods where it felt like it was getting better, even if it didn't completely go away?

Oh, um... well, like I was mentioning just a little bit ago, it's... it's been pretty much there this whole time. 

I really wish I could tell you there were a few good months in there where everything felt easy and light again. I try so hard to keep my energy up, especially for work, because my patients really need me to be present for them. I force myself to stay motivated to get my tasks done, so I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing. 

But that heavy feeling... where it just takes so much extra effort to do normal things... I don't think it's really let up for any real stretch of time. It's just sort of this constant background noise. I'm sorry, I know I'm probably just repeating myself now. I hope I'm not sounding too difficult or like a broken record. I'm trying to explain it as best as I can, is this helpful at all?
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable before you started feeling this way?

Well, um... I still try very hard to participate in things, you know? I still go to Sunday dinner with the family, and I try to look at the art I've always liked... I don't want anyone to think I'm withdrawing or being difficult. I really do make an effort to be present and cheerful for them.

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't sound ungrateful because I know I have a good life... most days, it just feels like the color has gone out of things. Even when I'm sitting right there at the table with everyone, or looking at something beautiful... I just feel this... this sadness. And I have to work so, so hard not to just tear up for no clear reason. I don't want to ruin the mood for anyone else, so I try to hide it. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I should be enjoying those things, shouldn't I? I really hope you don't think I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I'm trying to be better, I really am. Is it okay that I'm feeling this way?
Would you say that your feelings of sadness are interfering with your daily life most of the time, or is it more that they are just there in the background?

Well, um... I really try not to let it interfere, you know? I still show up for all my shifts, and I make sure my clients are safe and cared for. I don't want you to think I'm doing a bad job or letting anyone down. 

But... I guess it's more than just being in the background. It's... well, I've noticed I'm starting to fall behind on my client documentation. I always get it done eventually, I promise! It just takes me so much longer now. And... I used to volunteer to mentor the newer aides, but I just haven't been doing that lately. 

It's just that keeping up with the basics at work, and then making sure things are okay at home... it just takes everything I have right now. There's nothing left over. I feel terrible about the paperwork and not helping the new girls, I really do. I'm trying to get back on top of it. Does that make sense? I hope that answers your question okay.
Would you say that there are times when your sadness is much worse than others, or is it pretty consistent?

Oh, um... well, I try very hard to keep things steady, you know? I don't want to be unpredictable for the people around me, especially my clients. So... I wouldn't say there are times where it gets, like, dramatically worse or anything like that. 

It's really just... pretty consistent. Just that same sort of heavy feeling all the time. I mean, maybe if I'm really exhausted after a long shift it might feel a tiny bit harder to push through, but... mostly it just stays the same. I don't have big breakdowns or anything, I promise. I always keep it together. 

I hope I'm explaining that right. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I know I manage okay most days. Is that what you were asking?
Has this current period of feeling sad and disconnected from things been going on for more than two years, or is it something that has worsened or changed over the past two years?

Well, um... I really don't want to complain, because family is so important, you know? And I love my mother-in-law, I really do. We're happy to have her. But... if I think about when this really started feeling like this... it's been a little over two years now. Right around the time she moved in with us. 

I feel so guilty even saying that out loud. It's not her fault at all, she's a lovely woman and she needs our help. I just... I think the adjustment was harder on me than I expected, and then this feeling just sort of settled in and never left. It hasn't really gotten worse, it's just... been there ever since. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible daughter-in-law. I really do my best to make sure she's comfortable and happy here. Is it normal that a change like that would trigger something like this for so long?

doctor.question: Has this current period of feeling sad and disconnected from things been going on for more than two years, or is it something that has worsened or changed over the past two years?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on since my mother-in-law moved in with us a little over two years ago.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timeline of the symptoms, specifically whether they have been going on for more than two years.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I really don't want to complain, because family is so important, you know? And I love my mother-in-law, I really do. We're happy to have her. But... if I think about when this really started feeling like this... it's been a little over two years now. Right around the time she moved in with us. 

I feel so guilty even saying that out loud. It's not her fault at all, she's a lovely woman and she needs our help. I just... I think the adjustment was harder on me than I expected, and then this feeling just sort of settled in and never left. It hasn't really gotten worse, it's just... been there ever since. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible daughter-in-law. I really do my best to make sure she's comfortable and happy here. Is it normal that a change like that would trigger something like this for so long?

inference.note: F32.0 was ruled out due to the duration of symptoms being over two years, which is more consistent with F33.0

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent sadness, lack of motivation, and loss of interest in activities they once enjoyed, along with changes in appetite and sleep patterns, have been present for more than two years, meeting the criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia).
